grants.summary: Non-U.S. journalists, media researchers and academics can apply through their home country's Fulbright Commission or the U.S. Embassy for a Visiting Scholar grant to lecture, research or complete a professional project in journalism, media or broadcasting at a U.S. host institution. Award categories include 'Journalism/Media,' 'Journalism and Broadcasting' and 'Journalism (Research),' plus country-specific awards such as the Japan Journalism Research Award for junior and senior journalists.

amount.note: Benefits described as a monthly base stipend plus living/housing and travel allowances; exact figures vary by country and were not itemized in the material read.

grants.notes: Today's snapshot of foreign.fulbrightonline.org (2124 words, fetched today) covers only the Fulbright Foreign STUDENT Program and the FLTA programme for degree-seeking students; it does not mention a Journalism/Media award category at all, and only points non-US professors to a separate 'Fulbright Scholar Award' page on fulbrightscholars.org. The journalism/media-specific Visiting Scholar awards this entry describes are confirmed only via WebSearch (e.g. an IJNet listing on journalism-specific awards, plus country-specific Fulbright Commission pages). Each country/Commission sets its own cycle and deadline rather than one global deadline (e.g. Ukraine's most recent documents-submission deadline was 15 Oct 2025; Romania's general, non-journalism-specific Visiting Scholar deadline for 2027-28 is 5 Nov 2026), so no single deadline can be recorded. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.summary: An annual programme for established U.S. news organisations with a proven business model and a credible plan to expand into a new market, providing roughly $100,000 in grant funding alongside a year of business coaching (delivered via Blue Engine Collaborative) to support the expansion.

amount.note: Secondary coverage of the 2026 cycle describes three grant tiers — $400,000, $300,000 and $150,000 — superseding the previously recorded flat ~$100,000 figure, plus a year of coaching from Blue Engine Collaborative. Not directly confirmed on the funder's own page today.

grants.notes: US-only (not global) despite the source's declared global scope — eligibility is restricted to U.S.-based news organisations. Sources disagree on the exact 2026 round deadline (one Google-hosted page variant says 7 May, another says "Tuesday, May 20" — the two don't reconcile, so the previously recorded 7 May date is kept rather than guessing). That round has passed; the programme runs annually and a new round is expected but dates were not found. Amount updated today from a flat ~$100,000 figure to three reported tiers ($150k/$300k/$400k) per secondary coverage of the 2026 cycle. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.funder: Google News Initiative (via JournalismAI / Polis, LSE)
grants.summary: A GNI-supported programme funding news publishers to build and integrate AI-powered prototypes into newsroom workflows over an approximately nine-month programme, with mentoring alongside the funding. The most recent (second) cohort supported 12 publishers from 11 countries with grants reported at $50,000 or $100,000 each, running from around February 2026.

amount.note: Reported grant sizes for the 2025-2026 cohort; not directly confirmed on the funder's own page today.

grants.notes: This is a competitive but genuinely fund-for-future-work programme (selected publishers get grants + mentoring to build prototypes), not a prize for past work, so it was recorded despite the 'challenge' name. The most recent round's application deadline (3 Dec 2025) has passed and the next round's dates were not found. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.programme: One-year fellowship for politically persecuted individuals
grants.summary: A one-year, non-competitive fellowship offering safe housing, living expenses and a professional network in Hamburg to individuals — including journalists — who are persecuted in their home country for their commitment to democracy, freedom or human rights.
grants.eligibleActivity: The foundation's stated mission is protecting politically persecuted people broadly, not journalists specifically — but journalists are named as one of the recognised categories of fellows (past guests featured on the funder's page include reporters Omar Radi and Islam Shikhali), alongside artists, scientists and civil-society activists. A journalist facing political persecution can be proposed via the foundation's partner network for a year of safe housing in Hamburg while continuing their journalistic work.

amount.note: Covers housing, care and living expenses in Hamburg for one year; no specific figure stated.

grants.notes: Today's snapshot of the funder's own page carried only homepage narrative (guest bios, donation appeal) with no application or eligibility detail, so this record relies on search results. Applications appear to be accepted on a rolling basis, typically via referral from partner organisations (OSCE, PEN Centre, Amnesty International, German and foreign diplomatic missions, Reporters Without Borders) rather than a direct open call. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.funder: Hubert H. Humphrey Fellowship Program (Fulbright / J. William Fulbright Foreign Scholarship Board, U.S. Department of State)
grants.summary: A non-degree fellowship bringing accomplished, mid-career professionals from designated countries to a US host university for 10 months of graduate-level coursework, professional development and mentoring, plus a six-week professional affiliation with a US organization. Communications/Journalism is one of the designated fields of study; applications are submitted through the applicant's home-country U.S. Embassy, each on its own country-specific deadline.

amount.note: No stipend figure published; program reportedly covers tuition and university fees, a monthly maintenance allowance, a book/supplies allowance, a computer subsidy, round-trip international travel to the host institution, domestic travel to a Washington, D.C. seminar, and supplementary funds for professional activities. Funding does not extend to dependents/family members.

grants.notes: Reconfirmed on today's own-page snapshot (2391 words). Applicants apply via their country's U.S. Embassy Public Affairs Section or Binational Fulbright Commission; deadlines vary by country, with embassies/commissions submitting nominations to IIE by mid-September (already passed for this cycle). Fellows are selected by March and begin in the U.S. between August and September. Requires 5+ years full-time professional experience and English proficiency (TOEFL, with IELTS/Duolingo alternatives in some cases). Not journalism-specific — journalism is one of several eligible fields of study.

grants.funder: ICORN — International Cities of Refuge Network
grants.summary: A temporary protective residency programme, typically two years, for writers, journalists and artists who face persecution because of their work and cannot continue it safely in their home country or region.

amount.note: A grant covering living costs and accommodation, plus travel expenses related to relocation; no specific figure stated. Free of charge to applicants — no application or advisory fees.

grants.notes: The funder's own page states it is currently assessing a backlog of already-received applications and is not accepting new applications; new calls will be announced on its site. Standard residency length is two years, hosted across 92 ICORN member cities in Europe and the Americas.

grants.programme: CARAVAN — cross-border content grants for Central Asia
grants.summary: Grants for cross-border teams of journalists, media outlets, production studios and civil society organisations to produce content promoting regional cooperation and countering disinformation and hate speech across Central Asia, under the EU-funded CARAVAN project (Cultivating Audience Resilience through Amplification of Vibrant and Authentic Narratives).

amount.note: Up to €10,000 per cross-border team for applicants from Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan and Tajikistan; in Uzbekistan, individual participants receive fellowship-style support up to €10,000 instead.

grants.notes: No snapshot exists for internews.org/opportunities/ (never fetched). Found via IJNet/fundsforngos listings describing applications accepted 'on a rolling basis until May 31' with an interim deadline of March 17; a fundsforngos mirror dated this cycle to 30-Jun-2025, so the year this rolling window applies to is not confirmed, and no 2026 reopening was independently found today. Requires cross-border teams from at least two Central Asian countries, each team member with 1+ year of content-production experience. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.programme: FAIR Media Ukraine — Building Stronger Frontline Media and Informed Communities
grants.summary: An EU-funded grant programme inviting Ukrainian media outlets from eleven frontline regions (Donetsk, Luhansk, Kharkiv, Sumy, Chernihiv, Zaporizhzhia, Kherson, Mykolaiv, Odesa, Dnipropetrovsk and Kyiv) to produce frontline and investigative reporting for their communities.

amount.note: Average grant amount around EUR 15,000 per project, for projects lasting up to eight months.

grants.notes: No snapshot exists for this source; found via the EU Delegation to Ukraine's own announcement and imi.org.ua corroboration. Deadline (11 May 2026, 18:00 Kyiv time) has already passed, so this round is closed; no next round found today. Not confirmed via an automated fetch of Internews' own page (WebFetch blocked).

grants.programme: Strengthening Independent Media (SIM): Ukraine Content Production Grants (RFA-01)
grants.summary: Subgrants to independent Ukrainian media outlets for content production aimed at countering Russian disinformation and sustaining citizens' access to trusted, timely information.

amount.note: At least 10 subgrants of up to USD 50,000 each; performance period of 3-6 months, with no subgrant extending beyond 31 October 2026.

grants.notes: No snapshot exists for this source; found via Internews' own RFA-01 announcement page and corroborating trackers (fundsforngos, imi.org.ua). Deadline (17 April 2026, 12:00 Kyiv time) has already passed and the funded performance period runs no later than 31 October 2026, so this round is now closed; no next round found today. Not confirmed via an automated fetch of the funder's own page (WebFetch blocked).

grants.programme: Ukrainian Media and Society Fund — Sub-Grants for Media Coverage of Trafficking and Displacement
grants.summary: Subgrants to independent Ukrainian media and media organisations to produce ethical, accurate, human-centred multimedia journalism on the experiences of people from temporarily occupied territories, forced displacement, reintegration and social cohesion, alongside mentoring, training and access to research/analytics.

amount.note: Two tiers: up to UAH 520,000 for individual media/journalists and up to UAH 3,000,000 for media organisations.

grants.notes: Deadline 20 Sept 2026 passed the day before this check. This sits under Internews Ukraine's Ukrainian Media and Society Fund (UMSF), which runs as a rolling regranting mechanism with frequent, differently-themed rounds through the year — e.g. a civic-participation round (up to $4,000, deadline 20 Apr 2026) and the original UMSF launch round (up to UAH 600,000, deadline 26 Jan 2026) were also found, both closed and not recorded separately here. Check internews.ua/en/opportunity for the next round. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.funder: International Press Institute (IPI), funded by the Helsingin Sanomat Foundation
grants.programme: IPI Journalism and Media Freedom Research Fellowship (Helsingin Sanomat Foundation)
grants.summary: A four-month fellowship based at IPI's Vienna headquarters (hybrid possible) for journalists, media/press-freedom experts, and advanced MA/PhD researchers or graduates, funded by the Finland-based Helsingin Sanomat Foundation. Fellows get mentorship, peer exchange and integration into IPI's global network while producing research on journalism and press freedom.

amount.note: Monthly stipend €1,870-2,600 depending on qualifications (€2,600 for master's/PhD/postdoc/early-career applicants), plus a one-time €250 travel stipend for the Helsinki-Vienna trip.

grants.notes: Re-confirmed today via WebSearch (ipi.media/programmes/ still refuses automated fetches, per sources.json's own note on this source) — independent listings again give the 16 Oct 2026 deadline, the same stipend figures, and the Finland-affiliation eligibility requirement, with fellowship start date 1 September 2026 and four-month duration at IPI Vienna. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.funder: International Press Institute (IPI), leading the Media Innovation Europe consortium, EU-funded
grants.programme: Media Innovation Europe — Business Innovation Synergizer (Ukraine)
grants.summary: A Media Innovation Europe sub-programme offering grants of up to €30,000 to Ukrainian media organisations that already have tested plans for launching new products, services or monetisation models, to help build stronger products, services and digital solutions for long-term sustainability.
grants.notes: Found via an EU Neighbours East listing, cross-referenced against IPI's Media Innovation Europe consortium (which explicitly targets Ukrainian media under this sub-programme). Deadline 20 Sept 2026 has passed. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.funder: International Press Institute (IPI), leading the Media Innovation Europe consortium (with Thomson Media, The Fix Foundation and BIRN), EU-funded
grants.programme: Media Innovation Europe — Transition Accelerator (third edition)
grants.summary: Grants of up to €25,000 for up to 18 established European newsrooms investing in business-model transition, plus 8 months of online group training, personalised coaching and a 3-day in-person bootcamp in Vienna. Since 2022 the wider Media Innovation Europe programme has distributed over €1.2 million in grants to more than 100 independent media organisations.

amount.note: Up to €25,000 per newsroom, for up to 18 newsrooms, plus non-cash coaching/training support.

grants.notes: Third edition; this round's applications closed 9 Sept 2026. Programme is annual/recurring — check ipi.media/innovation/media-innovation-europe for the next call. No snapshot exists for this source (ipi.media/programmes/ was not in today's capture or failure list). Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.funder: International Press Institute (IPI), leading the Media Innovation Europe consortium, EU-funded
grants.programme: Media Innovation Europe — Validation Booster (third edition)
grants.summary: A six-month acceleration programme, part of Media Innovation Europe, open to journalists, media organisations, content creators, media initiatives or media-tech developers to test, refine and validate new digital product, service or format ideas for the media sector.

amount.note: Funding/grant figure for Validation Booster specifically was not stated in the material read (only the Transition Accelerator's €25,000 cap was).

grants.notes: Third edition; this round's applications closed 2 Sept 2026. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.programme: IRE / NICAR / AccessFest Conference Fellowships & Scholarships
grants.summary: A set of named funds that cover travel, registration and membership costs for journalists to attend IRE's conferences (the IRE Conference, NICAR and AccessFest), each with its own eligibility rules — some restricted to U.S. journalists, students, TV reporters, or specific beats such as immigration or rural news. The NICAR 2027 round is open now.

amount.note: NICAR27 fellowships (open now): complimentary conference registration ($100-$350 value), travel stipend (up to $500), one-year IRE membership/renewal ($25-$75 value). Other named funds in this cycle typically covered IRE membership (up to $75), conference registration, and for several funds four hotel nights (roughly $932-$1,100) plus a travel stipend ($500-$650); these are travel/attendance grants, not cash awards.

grants.notes: UPDATED this sweep from the funder's own page: 'NICAR Conference Fellowships — Applications for fellowships to attend NICAR27 are currently open! The deadline to apply is January 4, 2027 at 11:59 p.m. ET.' This is the live, open round as of today. Named funds feeding into this and the (now-closed, for this cycle) IRE Conference/AccessFest rounds include Eric B. Sager, Godfrey Wells Stancill, Sandra Thomas Environmental, Susan Carroll, Apples & Oranges, Diversity, Napoli Management Group TV, Jennifer Leonard, James Richard Bennett, David Donald, Gary Marx, Ottaway, Holly Whisenhunt Stephen, and R-CAR (the last two newly seen in today's crawl; R-CAR is for U.S. professional journalists at small, rural-audience outlets and freelancers serving rural communities, and requires a separate application). AccessFest 2026 ran October 8-10, 2026 (application window already closed before the event); the NICAR 2026 (March 2026) and IRE Conference 2026 (June 2026) rounds have also passed for this year's cycle. Next IRE Conference/AccessFest application windows not yet announced.

grants.summary: Supports nonfiction investigative reporting projects by journalists who make their living primarily as freelancers, intended for projects that demonstrate impact, breadth and significance.

amount.note: Amount not stated in evidence reviewed.

grants.notes: Re-confirmed verbatim on today's own-page snapshot: 'IRE's Freelance Fellowship supports nonfiction projects which demonstrate impact, breadth, and significance... This application is currently closed.' No reopening date given. Unlike most other IRE funds, the text captured does not state a nationality restriction, but confirm this on the funder's page before assuming it is open outside the U.S. Similar closed, currently-undated IRE project grants seen today: the Koch Continuum Grant in Public Health and Disability Investigative Reporting ($10,000 cash award), the David Dietz Fellowship (financial investigative journalism, under 10 years' experience) and the Chauncey Bailey Journalist of Color Investigative Reporting Fellowship.

grants.summary: A nine-month residential fellowship in Cambridge, Massachusetts for 10 science journalists worldwide to deepen expertise in a science, health, technology or environmental specialty while auditing MIT and Harvard courses. Open to full-time staff or freelance journalists with at least three years of science/health/tech/environment reporting experience.

amount.note: Stipend of $85,000 disbursed over 9.5 months, plus additional support for travel, housing and basic health insurance for fellows and their families.

grants.notes: Reconfirmed via today's own-page snapshot (896 words): program unchanged, no new cycle deadline announced. The 2026-2027 cycle opened 15 Nov 2025 and closed 9 Jan 2026 (already passed); those fellows are currently in residence. Applicants must not have completed a fellowship of four months or longer in the two years prior. Next cycle (2027-2028) likely opens around November 2026, based on the annual pattern, but no confirmed date yet on today's snapshot.

grants.summary: MDIF provides loans, equity investments, loan guarantees and related business advisory support to independent media and information businesses operating in countries with a history of media oppression, ownership concentration, a state of democratic transition, or information poverty. This is investment capital rather than grant funding; applicants must be independent of government or other interest groups, complete an inquiry form, and go through a multi-step due-diligence process. A current sub-line, MDIF Ventures, invests in young/growing media companies with social impact and scaling potential, and a regional Western Balkans Fund window has also been reported.

amount.note: MDIF Ventures is reported to offer ongoing funding up to US$1,000,000 per investee; main MDIF financing is case-by-case with no published general range. MDIF's overall portfolio has been reported at roughly $118.7M across ~58-60 media businesses in 31-34 countries in prior reporting.

grants.notes: Reconfirmed via WebSearch: MDIF remains an investment fund (debt/equity), not a grantmaker — financing carries repayment or ownership terms. No snapshot of the funder's page was available this run. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.summary: Media Defence provides legal grants and practical support for the defence of journalists, citizen journalists and media outlets facing prosecution or civil suits connected to their work. Applications for case support are usually made by the lawyer handling the case but can also be made by the journalist, their family or friends, or a relevant support organisation. Media Defence combines financial assistance with practical support to organisations that have, or wish to establish, a legal aid unit for journalists.

amount.note: Covers legal costs case-by-case; no published amount range found.

grants.notes: No snapshot was available for mediadefence.org (fetch never produced a file), so this entry is built from web search of the funder's own site pages (apply-for-case-support/, get-help/). Today's search also found Media Defence runs separate, time-bound 'litigation surgery' training workshops for lawyers (e.g. a Sub-Saharan Africa surgery held 2-4 October 2026 in Nairobi, application deadline 27 July 2026) — these are training events for lawyers, not grants to journalists, so not recorded as a separate entry. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.programme: Partner support for legal aid organisations
grants.summary: Media Defence funds and supports partner organisations that operate, or want to establish, a legal aid unit providing free legal support to journalists, citizen journalists and media outlets facing legal threats. In 2025 it reported awarding over £350,000 in grants to 19 partner organisations running media-defence centres across Europe, Latin America, Africa, Asia, and the Middle East/North Africa, enabling litigation of hundreds of freedom-of-expression cases.

amount.note: £350,000+ distributed across 19 partner organisations in 2025 in aggregate; no per-grant figure published. Past special regional calls (e.g. South East Asia) have offered up to GBP 25,000 for a 12-month partnership.

grants.notes: CHANGED from open to closed. Today's snapshot of mediadefence.org/become-a-partner/ states verbatim: 'We are not receiving applications at the moment. Please note decisions are based on the grantmaking selection criteria ... and availability of funding. We publish special calls for applications under the News section of our website.' The entry was previously held open on medium-confidence web-search evidence only; the funder's own page now directly contradicts that. The separate case-support programme for individual journalists (media-defence-legal-support) is unaffected and remains open — its own apply page ('Apply for Case Support') carries no such caveat and still says 'Apply Now'.

grants.summary: PULSE, n-ost's cross-border journalism network ('Europe beyond the beat'), funds small reporting teams of two journalists from different eligible countries to produce collaborative stories under one of four Thematic Networks (media and society, media/AI legislation, digitalisation, and disinformation/fact-checking). The 2026 call's pitch deadline (extended to 20 July 2026) has passed; n-ost's own site now also advertises 'PULSE 2026: New Formats & Open Calls' (published 23 Sep 2026) describing a shift toward fixed-deadline 'Sprint Stories'/'Deep Dive Series' calls, but no page with full details on amounts or exact dates was captured this round.

amount.note: Grant amount per team was not stated in any evidence read.

grants.notes: Re-checked today: the stale-yesterday snapshot (2026-10-18) again only shows the 'PULSE 2026: New Formats & Open Calls Now Live!' headline (published 23 Sep 2026) without full page text, and a WebSearch for the new Sprint Stories/Deep Dive Series formats and their deadlines returned no relevant results. No separate entry created for the new-format calls pending confirmed details. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.funder: n-ost (with Aktion Hoffnung fur Osteuropa and Renovabis)
grants.programme: Research Prize for Eastern Europe 2026 (Recherchepreis Osteuropa)
grants.summary: A 13th annual research grant, awarded by the Protestant 'Aktion Hoffnung fur Osteuropa' and Catholic 'Renovabis' organisations with n-ost as journalism-network partner, funding one or two in-depth, travel-intensive reporting projects (total up to EUR 7,000) on social and everyday-life issues in Central, South-Eastern and Eastern Europe, for publication in German-language media.

amount.note: Up to EUR 7,000 total, split across one or two funded reports, based on submitted budget.

grants.notes: Carried forward unchanged from the prior run; this round's deadline (31 Jan 2026) has passed and next round not yet announced. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.summary: A year-long fellowship for journalists of color combining monthly virtual skills-building sessions, D.C.-based training and mentor matches with veteran journalists, aimed at supporting retention and advancement in U.S. newsrooms.

amount.note: Free training and mentoring; no cash stipend mentioned on the funder's page.

grants.notes: The 2026 cohort (15 journalists) has already been selected; today's snapshot of the funder's own page states no application window or deadline for the next round. NPF also runs several other themed annual fellowships recruiting cohorts the same way (Local Business Journalism, Healthcare, International Trade, Workplace Mental Health, Rare Disease Reporting) plus the year-long Paul Miller Washington Reporting Fellowship for DC-based reporters — none had an open call with a stated deadline on today's page. NPF's other current listed calls (Easterseals, U.S. Chamber, AARP, Wounded Warrior, Bradlee, Dirksen, Berryman awards) are prizes for already-published work, not funding, and are excluded per site rules.

grants.summary: A Dutch government fund supporting civil-society human rights work worldwide, disbursed mainly through periodic country-specific calls run by individual Dutch embassies. Priority themes include preventing attacks on and obstacles to journalists and media workers, and the long-term sustainability of independent media outlets, alongside other human-rights themes (e.g. LGBTIQ+ equality, freedom of religion).
grants.eligibleActivity: This is a broad human-rights fund, not media-exclusive, but journalist safety and independent-media sustainability are named as stated priority themes within it. The 2026 Belarus-specific call explicitly lists 'preventing attacks on and obstacles to journalists and media workers' and 'long-term sustainability of Belarusian independent media outlets' as priorities, and the Sri Lanka 2026/27 call (up to EUR 20,000 per project) lists freedom of expression, internet freedom and independent journalism — so a media organisation can apply under these specific themes via the relevant embassy's open call.

amount.note: Amount varies by embassy/country call; the Sri Lanka 2026/27 call states funding of up to EUR 20,000 per project. No single global figure exists.

grants.notes: Funding is administered per-country through individual Dutch embassies/consulates, each running its own call with its own deadline; there is no single global deadline or application portal. A WebSearch today found several live/recent 2026 embassy-run rounds on official netherlandsandyou.nl and government.nl pages: a Hungary second round, a Sri Lanka 2026/27 round (up to EUR 20,000/project), and a Belarus 2026 round naming journalist safety and independent-media sustainability as priorities — confirming the fund and its media-relevant priorities are still active in 2026, though the Hungary round's own deadline could not be re-confirmed as still open. Interested applicants should check their nearest Dutch embassy's page. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.funder: Netherlands Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Embassy network)
grants.programme: MATRA — Netherlands Fund for Regional Partnerships
grants.summary: MATRA (maatschappelijke transformatie) funds local NGO-led projects in EU pre-accession countries and the Eastern Partnership that increase accountability and transparency of authorities, influence or monitor the implementation of policy and legislation, and support human rights, in the fields of rule of law, anti-corruption and democratic governance. Individual Dutch embassies (e.g. Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Kosovo) publish their own annual open calls, typically with two submission rounds per year.
grants.eligibleActivity: MATRA's own stated aim is to 'increase accountability and transparency of authorities, influence policies and legislation, and/or monitor their implementation' in rule-of-law and anti-corruption work. A journalism organisation registered as, or partnered with, a local NGO could apply for a documentation or monitoring project — e.g. investigative reporting on judicial reform or corruption that produces the public information the fund's own 'monitor implementation' criterion calls for — not an inferred fit.

amount.note: Per-project range found for the Serbia/Montenegro round; projects up to 24 months.

grants.notes: New entry — this source had no snapshot (never checked before) and no snapshot entry exists today, so this is built entirely from WebSearch. The Netherlands Embassy runs MATRA calls per country/embassy (evidence found for Serbia/Montenegro, Bosnia and Herzegovina, and Kosovo) with two annual submission rounds, 1 April and 1 August; both 2026 rounds have already passed with no confirmed 2027 dates yet, so status is set to closed rather than guessing a reopening date. Eastern Partnership-country rounds (per this source's configured scope) were not evidenced today. Only local NGOs may apply, not individual freelancers or unregistered outlets. Not confirmed on the funder's own page. Checked again today (2026-10-11): the source URL (government.nl/topics/grant-programmes) does not mention MATRA at all in its current content — it now lists only unrelated Dutch 'Focus' framework instruments (Mine Action, FemFocus, Focus on Freedom), none with a confirmed journalism/documentation route and all with passed deadlines. MATRA itself is confirmed via websearch to still run as country-level embassy calls administered via RVO (e.g. a Kosovo embassy call, EUR 50,000-80,000, no current deadline found), suggesting this source's URL should be repointed to RVO's MATRA page or a specific embassy's call page rather than the generic government.nl listing.

grants.funder: Royal Norwegian Embassy in Belgrade / Balkan Trust for Democracy (German Marshall Fund)
grants.programme: Support to 'Western Balkans 6' – Strengthening Media Freedom and Fighting Domestic and Gender-Based Violence
grants.summary: The Royal Norwegian Embassy in Belgrade co-funds, with the Norwegian Ministry of Foreign Affairs, a regional civil-society sub-granting scheme for the six Western Balkan countries, administered by the Balkan Trust for Democracy at the German Marshall Fund. The scheme awards project grants of $5,000-$75,000 under two windows: strengthening media freedom, and combating domestic and gender-based violence. Norway increased its funding to this programme in January 2026.
grants.eligibleActivity: One of the call's two funding windows is explicitly 'Media Freedom' (the other is domestic/gender-based violence), funded through the Norwegian Embassy's civil-society cooperation budget for the region and administered by BTD. A registered newsroom or media NGO in Serbia, or a regional outlet working across the WB6 countries, can apply directly under this window for a reporting, media-monitoring or media-sustainability project.

amount.note: BTD-administered grants; does not cover humanitarian assistance, infrastructure or equipment purchases.

grants.notes: Programme is funded via the embassy's civil-society cooperation budget but applied for and administered through the Balkan Trust for Democracy (German Marshall Fund); the embassy's own snapshot did not surface this detail and the exact current 2026 deadline window could not be confirmed. Not confirmed on the funder's own page. Checked again today (2026-10-11): no current-cycle deadline could be confirmed for this specific media-freedom window; the most recent confirmed related call under the same Balkan Trust for Democracy/German Marshall Fund umbrella (a media-literacy grants round, also Norwegian-embassy-linked) closed 16 June 2025, over a year ago, with no evidence of a newer round since. Kept open on the basis that the WB6 sub-granting mechanism itself is still described as active, but this should be re-verified directly on gmfus.org before the next cycle; confidence remains medium.

grants.programme: Healthy Information Sphere (International Human Rights Programme)
grants.summary: Oak Foundation's Healthy Information Sphere portfolio, within its International Human Rights Programme, supports independent journalism, media pluralism, digital rights and information integrity work aimed at holding power to account. Not-for-profit organisations not already invited by a programme officer may submit an unsolicited Letter of Enquiry through Oak's online form, though the Foundation states it has no open call for proposals and funds only a small share of the enquiries it receives.

amount.note: Not stated publicly; programme budgets are reported to be allocated roughly a year in advance and only a small number of unsolicited enquiries are funded each year.

grants.notes: Reconfirmed via WebSearch (no fresh snapshot available): the submit-enquiry online form remains Oak's only unsolicited intake mechanism; Oak responds within about two months if more information is needed or a formal proposal is invited. This is a general unsolicited-Letter-of-Enquiry intake, not a journalism-specific open call, and the Foundation has previously stated it has no open call for proposals at this time. Geographic focus reported as EU, US, UK, Brazil and other 'global East' geographies, so global scope is uncertain. Not confirmed on the funder's own page. Re-checked again today (2026-10-17) via a fresh oakfnd.org snapshot: Letter of Enquiry remains the only unsolicited intake route; still no open call for proposals. Unchanged.

grants.summary: An annual $5,000 award, established by ICFJ in memory of journalist and media-development consultant Hans Staiger, that lets one journalist already affiliated with OCCRP's global network pursue an investigative project of their choosing. Funds may cover travel, equipment, software, and contracts for experts or mentors; a panel selects one winning project per year.

grants.summary: Brings two journalists a year from countries with restricted press and information freedoms to Berlin for a six-month stay focused on rest, protection and recovery, for example after reporting from conflict zones or under state-security pressure. Run annually since 2015, and since 2026 organised independently by the taz Panter Stiftung in close cooperation with the Reporters Without Borders (RSF) fellowship programme.

amount.note: A monthly grant of EUR 1,000 for the six-month Berlin stay, per Reporters Without Borders Germany's fellowship page (reporter-ohne-grenzen.de); also covers visa/travel costs, a furnished Berlin apartment, travel health insurance, psychological support and training. Figure not found on taz's own page.

grants.funder: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Czech Republic
grants.programme: Transition Promotion Programme (TRANS) — Local Transition Projects
grants.summary: TRANS is the Czech MFA's framework for supporting human rights, democracy and civil-society development abroad. Local Transition Projects (LTPs) are run individually by Czech embassies and can fund work on rule of law, civic participation, and freedom of expression and information — including freedom of the media — implemented by non-governmental organisations.

amount.note: CZK 100,000-500,000 per-project range, confirmed today via several embassies' own 2026-round call pages on the mzv.gov.cz domain (e.g. New Delhi, Addis Ababa, Jakarta, Abuja), not from the main MFA overview page captured in yesterday's snapshot.

grants.notes: The programme is decentralised: each Czech embassy runs its own Local Transition (and, in some countries, explicitly 'Local Transition and Media') Project call with its own budget, exact themes and deadline. Yesterday's snapshot of the MFA's main English overview page just points to 'an overview of current grant calls' without listing terms itself; it was not re-fetched today. A WebSearch today found multiple embassies' 2026-round pages (New Delhi: India/Bhutan/Nepal/Maldives/Sri Lanka, deadline 30 Nov 2025; Addis Ababa: Ethiopia/Comoros/South Sudan, deadline 8 Jan 2026; Jakarta: Indonesia, deadline 31 Dec 2025; Abuja, deadline 30 Nov 2025; Manila/Lusaka, deadline 8 Dec 2025) — all now closed, with 2026 projects running roughly March-October 2026 and a CZK 500,000 ceiling (CZK 100,000-500,000 range) confirmed across several of them. No embassy has yet published a 2027 round as of today; last year's New Delhi page said its next call would be announced in autumn, which is now. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.
